resources.string: Ondo is a player: it shows the movies, series and channels of the subscription your provider gives you, and provides no content of its own.\n\nTo add your subscription, open Settings (the gear on Home, or tap the playlist name at the top of Home), Add a Playlist: an M3U link or file, or an Xtream Codes login (server address, user name and password). Tap a playlist in Settings to switch to it.

At the top of Home, tap the playlist’s name, shown with the time of its last update, to open your playlists in Settings; the magnifying glass opens Search and the gear opens Settings. The carousel below shows the best rated titles added in the last seven days, then Trending titles (with your TMDb token) and new releases.\n\nMovies in Progress and Series in Progress pick up where you stopped. To take a card out, long-press it (hold OK on a TV). Then come My List, New Movies and New Series (released this year or last year), Trending, then the channels: those in My List, or else the ones you watched last or the first ones of the playlist. A playlist with live channels only shows them first.

Many providers start category names with a code such as |PT| or FR:. The filter button on Movies, Series and Live TV (also in Settings, Languages and categories) hides a whole language or country at once, in every playlist; the categories the provider adds later follow the same rule.

Styles work the same way with the words of category names: hide Manga & anime, Children or Documentaries, or a word of your own such as Bollywood. Only category names count, not the genre of each movie.

You can also hide categories one by one there, and show them again at any time.

Categories whose name looks adult are hidden everywhere until you turn on Show adult categories in Settings.
When a stream does not play

Ondo says whether the provider, the network or the format is at fault.

If the provider refuses the stream, the subscription may have expired or too many devices may be watching at once: most providers allow one or two streams at a time.

If the server cannot be reached, check your connection and try again.

If the picture freezes now and then, More, Stream Statistics shows what arrives, what the video needs and whether the freezes come from the network or the provider, or from the player.

With a longer buffer (Settings, Buffer for live TV and Buffer for movies & series), the provider’s longer interruptions do not show, but the picture takes longer to appear.

In the player, More, Report a Problem… shows a report of the playback (start and seek times, freezes, statistics; no address, login or title) to send by mail or message, or in a GitHub issue.

Ondo has no account, no ads and no analytics of its own. Your playlists, history and settings stay on your device and are left out of device backups. Posters and the movie and series pages you have opened are kept on your device too, so that they show at once and open when the provider cannot be reached. When you turn on Sync on this network, your playlists, My List, collections, progress and TMDb token also go to your other Ondo devices on the same network, never through the internet.\n\nOndo connects to the servers you add and, once a week, to GitHub for the latest awards and festival selections (nothing about you is sent; turn off Update awards automatically in Settings). With your TMDb token, Ondo also asks TMDb for trending titles, background images and filmographies (only titles, years and names are sent).

Add to or remove from My List
In Live TV, long-press a channel to add it to My List.
Use My List on a movie or series page to find it here.
Use My List on an actor’s or a director’s page to find them here.

On a movie or series page, My List keeps it at hand. In Live TV, long-press a channel to add it to My List.

The My List tab gathers your movies, series and channels; search is the magnifying glass at the top of each screen.

Collections are your own groups, such as Weekend or Kids: use Collection on a movie or series page, then find them in My List, under Collections.

Movies, Series and Live TV show your provider’s categories. Search, the magnifying glass at the top of each screen, looks through channels, movies and series. In Search, the filter button keeps the movies and series released in the years you choose, or the movies of a festival or ceremony.\n\nIn a category, the sort button orders the posters by playlist order, name, date added, release date or rating. Movie pages show their awards and festival selections. Tap the name of a director or an actor on a movie or series page to see their other movies and series in your playlist: series always, movies among the pages you have opened. Genres, the year and awards open the titles of your playlist that share them the same way. Search also finds actors and directors by name.

Notifications are off for Ondo: allow them in Settings to be reminded.

The guide button on Live TV shows the programmes of the channels chosen there (My List, a category or all of them). The guide comes from your provider, or from the XMLTV address given when adding an M3U playlist.

Open an upcoming programme and set a reminder: a notification arrives a few minutes before it starts. The bell of the guide lists your reminders.

When your provider keeps an archive of a channel, open a past programme and choose Play replay; on the programme on now, Restart plays it from its start. A replay shows REPLAY in the player, and Back to live returns to the channel. A live channel paused for more than 10 seconds resumes where you paused it, from the archive.

Move with the arrows and press OK to choose. The menu is at the top of the tabs: the tabs, Search and Settings; it stays at the top of the screen as you scroll. Back closes a page; on a tab, it brings the page back to its top and the menu, then goes to Home, and Back in Home's menu leaves Ondo.

In the player, OK pauses, resumes and shows the controls (the Info key shows them too); Left and Right go back and forward 10 seconds where the stream allows it, otherwise they show the controls. The controls are large buttons: Play/Pause, back and forward 10 seconds, Subtitles and Audio, which list the tracks by language, Speed and More (Aspect ratio, Subtitle size, Sleep timer, Stream Statistics, Report a Problem…); the remote's subtitles and audio keys open their list directly. Up from the buttons reaches the progress bar: Left and Right move along it, faster when held, and the video goes there when you stop or press OK. Back closes a list, then the controls. On a live channel, Up and Down or the channel keys change channel, the number keys go straight to a channel, and the last-channel key returns to the one you watched before.

On a live channel, Channels lists the others with what is on now, and Restart plays the programme from its start when your provider keeps an archive; Back to live leaves a replay. At the end of an episode, Up next plays the next one: OK plays it now, Back declines. A film moves the TV to its own frame rate when the TV is set to match the content’s frame rate (display settings).

In Live TV, hold OK on a channel to add it to My List.

Tap the video to show or hide the controls. Double-tap the left or right side to go back or forward 10 seconds, and tap again to add 10 more; double-tap the middle to pause or resume. Hold a finger on the video to play twice as fast until you lift it. Slide up or down on the left side for the brightness, on the right side for the volume. Spread two fingers to fill the screen, pinch them to see the whole picture.

At the top: Picture-in-picture, Lock controls (the screen then ignores touches; tap it, then Unlock) and More (Subtitle size, Sleep timer, Stream Statistics, Report a Problem…). At the bottom: the progress bar, then Subtitles and Audio, which list the tracks by language, Speed and Aspect ratio. On a live channel, Channels lists the others with what is on now.

At the end of an episode, Up next plays the next one a few seconds later: Play now starts it at once, Cancel declines.

Playlists, My List, collections, progress and TMDb token

While Ondo is open, devices on this network with this setting on keep the same playlists, My List, collections, progress and TMDb token. iPhone, iPad and Mac sync through an Android device. Nothing leaves the local network, but playlist logins and the TMDb token travel unencrypted on it: turn this on at home only.
Looking for other devices with Ondo open…

Settings → Sync on this network keeps the same playlists, My List, collections, progress and TMDb token on your devices at home. Turn it on on each device and keep Ondo open on them: an Android TV, phone or tablet finds the others by itself; iPhone, iPad and Mac sync through an Android device. A device with no playlist yet can get yours this way: turn it on from the welcome screen.\n\nEverything goes directly from one device to another on your network, never through the internet. There is no pairing and logins and the TMDb token travel unencrypted on the network, so turn it on at home only. Other settings, hidden categories and playlists imported from a file stay on each device.

On themoviedb.org: your account → Settings → API. Copy the API Read Access Token (the long one); the API Key works too. This product uses the TMDB API but is not endorsed or certified by TMDB.
Movies are only found among the pages you have opened. Add your TMDb API Read Access Token in Settings to find all of them.

With your own TMDb token, Ondo adds a Trending row to Home with the titles of the moment that your playlist has, shows TMDb’s background image when your provider’s is missing or broken and photos of the cast on a title’s page, finds the people TMDb knows in Search, and lists all the movies of an actor or a director that your playlist has.\n\nOn themoviedb.org: your account → Settings → API. Copy the API Read Access Token (the long one; the API Key works too) and paste it in Settings, under TMDb: Ondo checks it with TMDb before saving it. With Sync on this network it reaches your other devices, so there is no need to type it with a remote. Only titles, years and names are sent to TMDb. This product uses the TMDB API but is not endorsed or certified by TMDB.
